title: 2D and 3D Figures: Quadrilaterals, Faces, Edges and Vertices
seo_title: Grade 3 2D and 3D Figures Worksheets: Quadrilaterals (TEKS 3.6A, 3.6B, STAAR)
standard_text: 3.6A classify and sort two- and three-dimensional figures, including cones, cylinders, spheres, triangular and rectangular prisms, and cubes, based on attributes using formal geometric language; 3.6B use attributes to recognize rhombuses, parallelograms, trapezoids, rectangles, and squares as examples of quadrilaterals and draw examples of quadrilaterals that do not belong to any of these subcategories
meta_desc: Free Grade 3 geometry worksheets for Texas TEKS 3.6A and 3.6B: name quadrilaterals, rhombuses, parallelograms, trapezoids, rectangles and squares, faces, edges and vertices of 3D figures, and nets. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Name a figure by its attributes: sides, angles, faces, edges and vertices.
key_sub: A square is also a rectangle and a rhombus. A cube has 6 faces, 12 edges and 8 vertices.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • A quadrilateral has 4 straight sides and 4 angles. Its name comes from its attributes, not from how it is turned.
  • Trapezoid: at least one pair of parallel sides. Parallelogram: 2 pairs of parallel sides. Rectangle: 4 right angles. Rhombus: 4 equal sides. Square: 4 equal sides and 4 right angles, so a square is also a rectangle and a rhombus.
  • Some quadrilaterals fit none of these names, like a kite or a shape with no parallel sides.
  • 3D figures have faces (flat surfaces), edges (where faces meet) and vertices (corners). A cube has 6 faces, 12 edges and 8 vertices. Cones, cylinders and spheres have curved surfaces.

Examples

Example

Is a square a rectangle?

A rectangle needs 4 right angles.

A square has 4 right angles.

Answer: Yes. Every square is a rectangle.

Example

How many faces does a triangular prism have?

2 triangle faces

3 rectangle faces

Answer: 5 faces

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Naming a shape by how it is turnedCheck the sides and angles. A turned square is still a square.
Thinking a square is not a rectangleA square has 4 right angles, so it is a special rectangle.
Mixing up a circle and a sphereA circle is flat (2D). A sphere is solid (3D).

faq.a: Classify and sort 2D and 3D figures, including cones, cylinders, spheres, triangular and rectangular prisms and cubes, by their attributes using formal geometric language.
Use attributes to recognize rhombuses, parallelograms, trapezoids, rectangles and squares as quadrilaterals, and draw quadrilaterals that are none of these.

faq.q: What is the difference between a face, an edge and a vertex?
faq.a: A face is a flat surface, an edge is a line where two faces meet, and a vertex is a corner where edges meet.

faq.q: Why can one shape have more than one name?
faq.a: Names describe attributes. A square has 4 equal sides (rhombus), 4 right angles (rectangle) and 2 pairs of parallel sides (parallelogram).

items.q: What is the best name for this shape? Use the marks.
items.e: The tick marks show 4 equal sides, and the small squares show 4 right angles. That makes it a square. It is also a rectangle and a rhombus, but square is the best name because it tells the most.

items.q: What is the best name for this shape? Use the marks.
items.e: The tick marks show 4 equal sides, so it is a rhombus. There are no right-angle marks, so it is not a square. Turning a shape does not change its name.

items.q: What is the best name for this shape? Use the marks.
items.e: The arrows show exactly one pair of parallel sides. The other two sides are not parallel, so it is a trapezoid.

items.q: A quadrilateral has exactly one pair of parallel sides. What is it called?
items.e: Exactly one pair of parallel sides: that is a trapezoid. Parallelograms, rectangles and rhombuses have 2 pairs.

items.q: A quadrilateral has 4 equal sides but no right angles. What is its best name?
items.e: 4 equal sides make it a rhombus. With no right angles, it is not a square.

items.q: What is the best name for this shape? Use the marks.
items.e: Opposite sides are equal (and parallel), but there are no right angles and the sides are not all equal. It is a parallelogram, not a rectangle or a rhombus.

items.q: On a drawing, what does a small square in a corner show?
items.e: A small square in a corner marks a right angle, a square corner like the corner of a book. Tick marks show equal sides, and arrows show parallel sides.

items.q: What is the best name for this shape? Use the marks.
items.e: The arrows show exactly one pair of parallel sides. The other two sides are not parallel, so it is a trapezoid.

items.q: What is the best name for this shape? Use the marks.
items.e: The tick marks show 4 equal sides, and the small squares show 4 right angles. That makes it a square. It is also a rectangle and a rhombus, but square is the best name because it tells the most. Turning a shape does not change its name.

items.q: What is the best name for this shape? Use the marks.
items.e: The tick marks show 4 equal sides, and the small squares show 4 right angles. That makes it a square. It is also a rectangle and a rhombus, but square is the best name because it tells the most. Turning a shape does not change its name.

items.q: What is the best name for this shape? Use the marks.
items.e: The small squares show 4 right angles, so it is a rectangle. The tick marks show that only opposite sides are equal, so it is not a square.

items.q: What is the best name for this shape? Use the marks.
items.e: The arrows show exactly one pair of parallel sides. The other two sides are not parallel, so it is a trapezoid. Turning a shape does not change its name.

items.q: What is the best name for this shape? Use the marks.
items.e: The small squares show 4 right angles, so it is a rectangle. The tick marks show that only opposite sides are equal, so it is not a square.

items.q: What is the best name for this shape? Use the marks.
items.e: The tick marks show 4 equal sides, so it is a rhombus. There are no right-angle marks, so it is not a square. Turning a shape does not change its name.

items.q: A quadrilateral has 4 equal sides and 4 right angles. What is its best name?
items.e: 4 equal sides and 4 right angles: that is a square. (It is also a rectangle and a rhombus, but square tells the most.)

items.q: What is the best name for this shape? Use the marks.
items.e: The tick marks show 4 equal sides, so it is a rhombus. There are no right-angle marks, so it is not a square.

items.q: On a drawing, what do matching tick marks on two sides show?
items.e: Sides with the same number of tick marks are the same length.

items.q: A quadrilateral has 4 right angles. Its opposite sides are equal, but its sides are not all the same length. What is its best name?
items.e: 4 right angles make it a rectangle. The sides are not all equal, so it is not a square.

items.q: What is the best name for this shape? Use the marks.
items.e: Opposite sides are equal (and parallel), but there are no right angles and the sides are not all equal. It is a parallelogram, not a rectangle or a rhombus. Turning a shape does not change its name.

items.q: What is the best name for this shape? Use the marks.
items.e: The small squares show 4 right angles, so it is a rectangle. The tick marks show that only opposite sides are equal, so it is not a square. Turning a shape does not change its name.

items.q: What does every square have that not every rhombus has?
items.e: Every rhombus already has 4 equal sides. A square is a rhombus that also has 4 right angles.

items.q: How many pairs of parallel sides does a parallelogram have?
items.e: A parallelogram has 2 pairs of parallel sides: top and bottom, and left and right. (4 is the number of sides, not pairs.)

items.q: A closed shape has 4 straight sides, and all 4 sides are the same length. Which name must fit it?
items.e: 4 equal sides is all a rhombus needs. It is a square only if it also has 4 right angles, and we do not know that.

items.q: Which shape has 4 equal sides?
items.e: Shape B has the same tick mark on all 4 sides. The others have 2 pairs of equal sides, not 4 equal sides.

items.q: Which shape has exactly one pair of parallel sides?
items.e: Shape D has arrows on only one pair of sides. The others have arrows on 2 pairs of sides.

items.q: How many right angles does this shape have?
items.e: All 4 corners have the right-angle mark. Every rectangle has 4 right angles, even when it is turned.

items.q: How many right angles does this shape have?
items.e: Only one corner has the right-angle mark. The other 3 angles are bigger or smaller than a right angle.

items.q: Which shape has 4 right angles?
items.e: Shape C has a right-angle mark in all 4 corners. One shape has only 2 right angles, and the others have none.

items.q: What do shape A and shape B both have?
items.e: Both are quadrilaterals with 4 sides. Only the rectangle has right angles, and only the rhombus has 4 equal sides.

items.q: How many right angles does every rectangle have?
items.e: A rectangle is a quadrilateral with 4 right angles. That is what makes it a rectangle.

items.q: What does every square have that not every rectangle has?
items.e: Every rectangle already has 4 right angles. A square is a rectangle that also has 4 equal sides.

items.q: Which attribute do a square and a rectangle always share?
items.e: Both have 4 right angles. A square also has 4 equal sides, but most rectangles do not.

items.q: What do shape A and shape B both have?
items.e: Both shapes have right-angle marks in all 4 corners. Only the square has 4 equal sides.

items.q: What does every rectangle have that not every parallelogram has?
items.e: All parallelograms have 2 pairs of parallel sides and 4 vertices. A rectangle is the kind with 4 right angles.

items.q: How many right angles does this shape have?
items.e: There are no right-angle marks. A rhombus has 4 equal sides, but its angles are not right angles unless it is a square.

items.q: How many sides of a rhombus are the same length?
items.e: A rhombus is a quadrilateral with 4 equal sides.

items.q: What do shape A and shape B both have?
items.e: Both shapes have the same tick mark on all 4 sides. Only the square has right angles.

items.q: How many right angles does this shape have?
items.e: The marks show right angles at 2 corners only. The other 2 angles are not right angles.

items.q: Which attribute does every quadrilateral have?
items.e: Every quadrilateral has 4 sides. Right angles, equal sides and parallel sides belong only to some quadrilaterals.

items.q: Which attribute do a square and a rhombus always share?
items.e: Both have 4 equal sides. A square also has 4 right angles, but most rhombuses do not.

items.q: Which quadrilateral is NOT a rectangle, a rhombus, or a square?
items.e: Shape C is a kite shape. Its sides come in 2 pairs of different lengths and it has no right angles. The others are a rhombus, a square and a rectangle.

items.q: A toy kite has 2 sides that are 30 cm long and 2 sides that are 50 cm long. Is it a rhombus?
c: Yes, it looks like a diamond
No, its sides are not all equal
items.e: A rhombus needs 4 equal sides. This kite has two 30 cm sides and two 50 cm sides. It is a quadrilateral, but not a rhombus.

items.q: Which quadrilateral is NOT a rectangle, a rhombus, or a square?
items.e: Shape C has 4 different side lengths and no right angles. The others are a rectangle, a rhombus and a square.

items.q: Leo draws a quadrilateral with exactly 1 right angle. Which of these names can it have?
items.e: Rectangles and squares need 4 right angles. If a rhombus has 1 right angle, all 4 of its angles are right angles. So a shape with exactly 1 right angle is none of these.

items.q: A picture frame has 4 sides of 10 inches and 4 right angles. Which names fit it?
items.e: 4 right angles make it a rectangle, 4 equal sides make it a rhombus, and both together make it a square. All three names fit.

items.q: Why is this shape not a rhombus?
c: Its sides are not all equal
items.e: A rhombus needs 4 equal sides. This rectangle has 2 long sides and 2 short sides. (A rhombus can have right angles: a square does.)

items.q: Why is this shape not a rectangle?
items.e: A rectangle needs 4 right angles. This parallelogram has none. Turning or size never decides a shape's name.

items.q: No sides are equal, no sides are parallel, and there are no right angles. What is the best name for this shape?
items.e: It has 4 straight sides, so it is a quadrilateral. With no parallel sides it is not a trapezoid or a parallelogram, and with no equal sides it is not a rhombus.

items.q: Zoe cuts one corner off a square piece of paper with one straight cut. How many sides does the paper have now?
items.e: The cut takes away 1 corner but adds 1 new side and 2 new corners: 4 + 1 = 5 sides. It is now a pentagon, not a quadrilateral.

items.q: Why is this kite shape not a rhombus?
c: Its sides are not all equal
items.e: The tick marks show 2 short equal sides and 2 long equal sides. A rhombus needs all 4 sides equal. A rhombus does not need right angles.

items.q: Why is this rhombus not a square?
items.e: The tick marks show 4 equal sides, but a square also needs 4 right angles. This shape has none.

items.q: A stop sign has 8 sides. Is it a quadrilateral?
items.e: A quadrilateral has exactly 4 sides. A stop sign has 8 sides, so it is an octagon.

items.q: A floor tile has 4 sides, and each side is 8 inches long. Its corners are not right angles. What is its best name?
items.e: 4 equal sides make a rhombus. Without right angles, it is not a square.

items.q: The bases on a baseball field make a shape with 4 equal sides of 90 feet and 4 right angles. People call it a diamond. What is its best name?
items.e: 4 equal sides and 4 right angles make a square. It looks like a diamond only because it is turned.

items.q: A window has 4 right angles. The top and bottom are 4 feet long, and the sides are 2 feet long. Which name does NOT fit?
items.e: It has 4 right angles, so it is a rectangle, a parallelogram and a quadrilateral. Its sides are not all equal, so it is not a square.

items.q: Which quadrilateral is NOT a rectangle, a rhombus, or a square?
items.e: Shape B is a trapezoid. It has no right angles and its sides are not all equal. The others are a square, a rectangle and a rhombus.

items.q: A door is 7 feet tall and 3 feet wide. It has 4 right angles. What is its best name?
items.e: 4 right angles make a rectangle. The sides are not all equal, so it is not a square.

items.q: A triangle-shaped sign is cut straight across, parallel to its bottom edge. What shape is the bottom piece?
items.e: The bottom piece has 4 sides. The cut and the bottom edge are parallel, but the two slanted sides are not. Exactly one pair of parallel sides makes a trapezoid.

items.q: A slice of pizza has 2 straight sides and a curved crust. Is it a quadrilateral?
items.e: A quadrilateral has 4 straight sides. The pizza slice has a curved side, and only 3 sides in all.

items.q: Mia wants to draw a quadrilateral that is not a rectangle, a rhombus, or a square. Which plan works?
items.e: With 4 different side lengths it cannot be a rhombus or a square. A rectangle needs opposite sides equal, so it is not a rectangle either.

sets.title: Faces, edges and vertices of 3D figures

items.q: A flat surface of a 3D figure is called a …
items.e: A face is a flat surface. An edge is where two faces meet. A vertex is a corner.

items.q: The line where two faces of an object meet is called an …
items.e: Where two faces meet there is an edge.

items.q: A corner of an object, where edges meet, is called a …
items.e: A corner is a vertex. More than one vertex are called vertices.

items.q: This is a cube. How many faces does it have?
items.e: A cube has 6 faces, 12 edges and 8 vertices. Some faces are at the back or underneath. You cannot see them, but you must count them too.

items.q: This is a cube. How many edges does it have?
items.e: A cube has 6 faces, 12 edges and 8 vertices. The dashed lines show edges at the back. Count them too.

items.q: This is a cube. How many vertices does it have?
items.e: A cube has 6 faces, 12 edges and 8 vertices. Some vertices are at the back, where the dashed lines meet. Count them too.

items.q: This is a rectangular prism. How many faces does it have?
items.e: A rectangular prism has 6 faces, 12 edges and 8 vertices. Some faces are at the back or underneath. You cannot see them, but you must count them too.

items.q: This is a rectangular prism. How many edges does it have?
items.e: A rectangular prism has 6 faces, 12 edges and 8 vertices. The dashed lines show edges at the back. Count them too.

items.q: This is a triangular prism. How many faces does it have?
items.e: A triangular prism has 5 faces, 9 edges and 6 vertices. Some faces are at the back or underneath. You cannot see them, but you must count them too.

items.q: This is a triangular prism. How many edges does it have?
items.e: A triangular prism has 5 faces, 9 edges and 6 vertices. The dashed lines show edges at the back. Count them too.

items.q: This is a triangular prism. How many vertices does it have?
items.e: A triangular prism has 5 faces, 9 edges and 6 vertices. Some vertices are at the back, where the dashed lines meet. Count them too.

items.q: This is a square-based pyramid. How many faces does it have?
items.e: A square-based pyramid has 5 faces, 8 edges and 5 vertices. Some faces are at the back or underneath. You cannot see them, but you must count them too.

items.q: This is a square-based pyramid. How many edges does it have?
items.e: A square-based pyramid has 5 faces, 8 edges and 5 vertices. The dashed lines show edges at the back. Count them too.

items.q: This is a square-based pyramid. How many vertices does it have?
items.e: A square-based pyramid has 5 faces, 8 edges and 5 vertices. Some vertices are at the back, where the dashed lines meet. Count them too. Do not forget the vertex at the top.

items.q: This is a triangle-based pyramid. How many faces does it have?
items.e: A triangle-based pyramid has 4 faces, 6 edges and 4 vertices. Some faces are at the back or underneath. You cannot see them, but you must count them too.
A cylinder has no corners, so it has 0 vertices. Its 2 edges are curved circles, not corners. In a drawing it can look like it has 4 corners, but it does not.
A cone has 1 vertex: the point at the top. Its circle edge is curved and has no corners.

items.q: Every face of a cube is a square. How many right angles does one face have?
items.e: A square has 4 square corners, so it has 4 right angles. 8 is the number of vertices of the whole cube.

items.q: Which object has right angles at every corner of every face?
items.e: All 6 faces of a rectangular prism are rectangles, and every rectangle has 4 right angles. Pyramids and triangular prisms have triangle faces, and a triangle can never have a right angle at every corner.

items.q: Sofia says a cube has 8 edges. She is wrong. What did she count?
items.e: A cube has 8 vertices (corners) and 12 edges. Sofia counted the vertices.

items.q: What shape is each face of a cube?
items.e: All 6 faces of a cube are squares of the same size. A cube is the 3D figure; its faces are 2D squares.

items.q: Which 2D shapes are the faces of a triangular prism?
items.e: A triangular prism has a triangle at each end (2 triangles) and 3 rectangles joining them: 5 faces.

items.q: Which 2D shapes are the faces of a square-based pyramid?
items.e: A square-based pyramid has 1 square at the bottom and 4 triangles that meet at the top: 5 faces.

items.q: Which 2D shapes are the faces of a triangle-based pyramid?
items.e: It has 3 triangles that meet at the top and 1 more triangle as the base: 3 + 1 = 4 triangles. Do not forget the base.

items.q: Which 2D shapes are the faces of a rectangular prism like a cereal box?
items.e: A rectangular prism has 6 faces and each one is a rectangle: front and back, top and bottom, and 2 ends.
The flat faces of a cylinder are circles. In a drawing they look like ovals because we see them from the side.

items.q: What shape is the flat face of a cone?
items.e: A cone has 1 flat face: a circle. From the side a cone looks like a triangle, but it has no triangle faces.

items.q: Nevaeh dips one face of a cube in paint and presses it on paper. What shape does she print?
items.e: Every face of a cube is a square, so the print is a square. A print is flat (2D), so it cannot be a cube.

items.q: Marcus traces around the bottom of a soup can. What shape does he draw?
items.e: The can is a cylinder and its bottom face is a circle, so the tracing is a circle.

items.q: You press each face of an object in paint. Which object can print a triangle?
items.e: A triangular prism has a triangle face at each end. A cube, a cylinder and a rectangular prism have no triangle faces.

items.q: Which object can print 1 square and 4 triangles?
items.e: A square-based pyramid has 1 square face and 4 triangle faces.

items.q: How many square faces does a square-based pyramid have?
items.e: Only the base is a square: 1 square face. The other 4 faces are triangles.

items.q: How many triangle faces does a triangular prism have?
items.e: A triangular prism has 1 triangle at each end: 2 triangles. Its name says “triangle”, but its other 3 faces are rectangles.

items.q: How many rectangle faces does a triangular prism have?
items.e: The 3 faces that join the 2 triangle ends are rectangles: 3 rectangles.

items.q: A net is a flat shape you can fold to make a 3D figure. How many squares are in a net of a cube?
items.e: A cube has 6 faces, so its net has 6 squares, one for each face. 8 is the number of vertices.

items.q: This net is folded up. Which 3D figure does it make?
items.e: 6 squares of the same size fold up into a cube: 1 square for each face.

items.q: This net is folded up. Which 3D figure does it make?
items.e: The square is the base. The 4 triangles fold up and meet at a point: a square-based pyramid.

items.q: This net is folded up. Which 3D figure does it make?
items.e: The 3 rectangles fold into a tube and the 2 triangles close the ends: a triangular prism.

items.q: This net is folded up. Which 3D figure does it make?
items.e: 6 rectangles that are not all squares fold into a rectangular prism, like a box.

items.q: This net is folded up. Which 3D figure does it make?
items.e: The rectangle rolls into a tube (the curved surface) and the 2 circles close the ends: a cylinder.
